Construct approximate EEG sensor adjacency from projected positions

Source: R/make_sensor_adjacency.R
make_sensor_adjacency.Rd

Builds a symmetric, named logical adjacency matrix using spatial k-nearest neighbors. To avoid connecting distant sensors, candidate edges longer than `distance_factor` times the median nearest-neighbor distance are omitted. The result is an *approximation* based on 2D positions; inspect the graph before scientific use.

Usage

make_sensor_adjacency(
  data,
  sensor_id = "sensor",
  spatial_id = c("xproj", "yproj"),
  k = 4L,
  distance_factor = 1.8,
  warn_disconnected = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing sensor names and projected locations. Repeated rows per sensor (e.g., a sensor-by-time prediction grid) are OK provided each sensor has a single consistent position.

sensor_id

Sensor identifier column (default `"sensor"`).

spatial_id

Two numeric spatial coordinate columns.

k

Number of nearest neighbors considered per electrode. The resulting undirected graph may have more than `k` edges per sensor.

distance_factor

Maximum candidate edge length divided by the median nearest-neighbor distance. Use `NULL` to disable filtering.

warn_disconnected

Issue a warning if the inferred graph has more than one connected component.

Value

Symmetric logical matrix with sensor names on both axes and `FALSE` on the diagonal.
